To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the mortality rate of liver cancer in 65 Chinese counties is correlated with the county-wide prevalence rate of hepatitis-B surface-antigen positivity and the plasma levels of total cholesterols and high consumption of rapeseed oil and mouldy corn.

liver cancer mortality in Chinese adults is correlated with the county-wide prevalence rate of chronic hepatitis B, plasma cholesterol levels, and the consumption of liquor, mouldy corn, and rapeseed.

hepatitis-B virus infection, high plasma cholesterol and high consumption levels of certain foods, including rapeseed oil and mouldy corn are associated with higher mortality from liver cancer in China.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between diet and cancer.
the role of diet and nutrition in liver cancer, and the possible mechanisms of action.
the relationship between dietary and biochemical factors and the risk of developing liver cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the major risk factor for liver cancer is hepatitis B, and the second major risk factor is dietary aflatoxin B 1.
the most important risk factors for hepatocellular carcinoma in China are hepatitis B virus infection, alcohol consumption, and aflatoxin exposure.
the major risk factor for liver cancer in China is chronic infection with hepatitis B, which may be modified by the dietary and nutritional factors that were examined.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the major cause of liver cancer mortality was chronic infection of the hepatitis B virus.
the most significant risk factor for liver cancer mortality is hepatitis B infection.

hepatitis B virus infection, high consumption of alcohol, high intake of cholesterol and rapeseeds oils and low intake of wheat are important factors that may explain the high mortality rate of liver cancer in Chinese population.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need to focus on the role of dietary factors in the etiology of liver cancer.
hepatitis B virus infection is a major risk factor for liver cancer in China.

the high rates of liver cancer in rural areas of China are not due to dietary factors, but to chronic hepatitis B virus infection, and that the best way to lower the incidence of liver cancer in these areas is to control hepatitis B infection.
